newsitem.title: USA: IMM currency futures erode more late, end lower.
newsitem.headline: IMM currency futures erode more late, end lower.

text.p: Most IMM currency futures eroded further as afternoon trading wound down, with lead-month contracts closing moderately to sharply lower.
Focus switched to the Swiss franc, which drooped to a big daily loss and stole the limelight from the mark.
Traders said dealers offered the Swiss unit much of the day, especially in the morning when it breached key support versus the dollar and on the mark cross in fairly busy trade.
"I think it was just the cross was so strong," said one floor broker of the Swiss franc's drop as the mark cut losses. "There was cross unwinding."
"It was a huge technical correction on the cross," added another floor broker.

Both nearby marks and Swiss francs set new contract lows Thursday, with the Swiss franc sliding through sell stops and then drawing "boatloads" of other sales when it punctured key support near $0.6740 or about 1.4925 spot, he added.
September marks, meanwhile, recouped from lows hit on early on ideas that German interest rates are on hold for a couple of weeks.
The Bundesbank left official rates unchanged and fixed its securities repurchase rate at 3.0 percent for two weeks.
That means the German central bank must revisit the repo rate issue at the middle of its four-week summer break.

Brokers said that fact helped temper mark sales, since the German central bank still could snug up credit conditions then to head off inflationary pressures tied to the mark's slide to multi-year lows against the U.S. dollar.
The dollar also proved unable clear the key 1.84 mark level, partly for fear of irritating the central banks enough to spark mark buying, some brokers added.
But others said they doubted the mark had dropped far enough yet to warrant an intervention watch.
The Bundesbank said it would keep a close eye on developments in financial markets in the future, as part of its observation of price developments.
"We were looking at 1.85 to bring in the Bundesbank," said a second broker. "I still don't think the Bundesbank is panicking. We'll see what they do in two weeks" with the repo rate.
A dollar rally to 1.85 marks would equate a fall in September mark futures to about $0.5424.
Some instead expected the dollar next to target 1.8427, or $0.5446 in September futures, just below Thursday's low.
Sterling fell after the Confederation of British Industry survey highlighted exporter concerns about sterling's strength, which overshadowed a narrowing in the British trade gap.
The bigger than expected drop in U.S. weekly jobless claims to 299,000, their lowest level in a year, also kept currencies moving to the downside near the outset.

September yen ended down $0.000036 at $0.008677, marks fell $0.0026 to $0.5468, Swiss francs skidded $0.0105 to $0.6666, sterling lost $0.0046 to $1.6708, Can dollar eased $0.0003 to $0.7260, Aussie dollar rose $0.0006 to $0.7378, and the Mexican peso rose $0.000575 to $0.125575.
